Build a Countdown app

Source: R/app-core.R
cd_app.Rd

Puts a whole Countdown app together and returns it as a Shiny app: the frame every app shares (header, sidebar, language picker), the Introduction and Load Data screens, and the app's own pages. An app's run_app() sets its options, builds its translator, lists its pages and its nav tree, and then calls cd_app(). See cd2030.rmncah::run_app() for a complete one.

Usage

cd_app(
  app_name,
  app_version,
  theme,
  nav_sections,
  registry,
  i18n,
  language,
  selected_file,
  upload_ui = get0("upload_data_ui", envir = parent.frame()) %||% cd_upload_data_ui,
  upload_server = get0("upload_data_server", envir = parent.frame()) %||%
    cd_upload_data_server
)

Arguments

app_name

The app's name, shown in the header.

app_version

The app's version, shown in the header.

theme

The app's colour theme: "rmncah" or NULL (maroon), "vaccine" (blue) or "pooled" (green).

nav_sections

The sidebar's nav tree: a list of nav sections, made with cd_nav_start() and the functions beside it, and with the kit's cd_nav_section() and cd_nav_item().

registry

The app's pages: a list of page definitions made with the kit's cd_page_def(), the same list the app gives to cd_use_pages().

i18n

The app's translator (a shiny.i18n translator), used for every label.

language

The language the app starts in, for example "en", "fr" or "pt".

selected_file

The path of a dataset to open when the app starts, or NA for none. DataSuite gives it when the app is started on a file.

upload_ui

The ui function of the Load Data screen, called as upload_ui("upload_data", i18n = i18n, is_electron = ), where is_electron is TRUE when selected_file is given. By default it is the function named upload_data_ui where cd_app() is called from, when there is one, and otherwise the shared screen, cd_upload_data_ui(), which the app sets up with options(cd2030.wizard = ).

upload_server

The server function of the Load Data screen, called as upload_server("upload_data", i18n, selected_file, active = ). It must return a list with cache (a reactive that returns the dataset, a CacheConnection, or NULL before one is loaded) and requires_walkthrough (a reactive that is TRUE for a new upload and FALSE for a dataset opened again). By default it is the function named upload_data_server where cd_app() is called from, when there is one, and otherwise cd_upload_data_server().

Value

A Shiny app object. Printing it, or passing it to shiny::runApp(), runs the app.

Details

cd_app() calls the kit's datasuite.ui::app_frame() and adds what is the same in every Countdown app:

  • The Introduction screen and the Load Data screen. The app opens on Load Data, and these two screens are never locked.

  • The dataset. It is the reactive the Load Data screen returns, and every page receives it as cache. The pages unlock once the dataset holds Countdown data. The nav items marked requires_adjustment = TRUE unlock once the data is also adjusted.

  • The row naming the denominators in use, in every page header (cd_denominator_header()).

  • The language. A dataset that has just been uploaded takes the language on screen, and a dataset that is opened again shows the language it was saved with.

  • The reports' colours, which follow theme.

  • What DataSuite's chat can read and do in the app: the filters of the page on show, the dataset, and actions that set filters and save, read, change and write reports.

Before calling it, the app registers its translator with cd_use_i18n() and its pages with cd_use_pages().

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
i18n <- shiny.i18n::init_i18n(translation_json_path = cd_translations("translation.json"))
cd_use_i18n(i18n)

pages <- my_pages()
cd_use_pages(pages)

cd_app(
  app_name = "My Countdown app", app_version = "1.0.0", theme = "vaccine",
  nav_sections = list(cd_nav_start(), cd_nav_quality(), cd_nav_denominators()),
  registry = pages, i18n = i18n, language = "en", selected_file = NA
)
} # }
